findings.title: isCustomDashboard always false on first render
findings.problem: `isCustomDashboard` is evaluated synchronously as `dashboards.some((d) => d.id === tab)`, but `dashboards` is `[]` in the Valtio store until the `loadDashboards()` call in the startup `useEffect` resolves. On every initial render of a custom-dashboard URL the expression returns false.
findings.impact: The 'Edit Dashboard' button is absent on first render and then flashes in after the async load completes, producing a layout shift for any user navigating directly to a saved custom dashboard tab.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a `dashboardsLoaded` boolean flag (state or store field) set to true after `loadDashboards()` resolves; gate `isCustomDashboard` on that flag being true before evaluating `dashboards.some(...)`.

findings.title: Adoption redirect collides with custom-dashboard id
findings.problem: The `useEffect` redirects unconditionally when `tab === 'adoption'` without checking whether a custom dashboard with that exact id exists in `dashboards`. While `createDashboard` uses `crypto.randomUUID()` ensuring new dashboards cannot have id 'adoption', any legacy persisted entry or direct localStorage manipulation could create a collision. Reachability unconfirmed — no such dashboard is known to exist.
findings.impact: A user with a custom dashboard whose stored id equals 'adoption' would be permanently redirected away from it on every navigation, with no recovery path short of directly editing localStorage.
findings.recommendation: Change the redirect condition to `if (tab === 'adoption' && !dashboards.some((d) => d.id === 'adoption'))`, or document 'adoption' as a reserved id and add a guard in `createDashboard`/`loadDashboards` to reject or rename any entry with that id.

findings.title: Retirement notice missing ARIA live-region semantics
findings.problem: The retirement notice `<div>` injected when `notice === 'adoption-retired'` carries no `role="alert"` or `aria-live` attribute. The notice is dynamically inserted into the DOM after the adoption-tab redirect fires.
findings.impact: Screen-reader users redirected from `?tab=adoption` receive no auditory notification of the retirement message, violating WCAG SC 4.1.3 (Status Messages). The redirect itself is also not announced.
findings.recommendation: Add `role="alert"` to the outer `<div>` of the notice banner (or `aria-live="polite"` if a less assertive announcement is preferred), so the message is read aloud when it appears.

findings.title: vi.mock targets wrong AnalyticsWidget module path
findings.problem: `vi.mock('../AnalyticsWidget', ...)` is resolved from the `__tests__/` directory, pointing to `widgets/AnalyticsWidget` (which does not exist). `DynamicWidget.tsx` imports `'../AnalyticsWidget'` from `widgets/`, resolving to `components/AnalyticsWidget`. The two resolved paths are different module IDs, so Vitest never intercepts the real import and the mock is dead.
findings.impact: The 'Metric no longer available' assertion passes only because the real `AnalyticsWidget` happens to render `error.message`. Any future change to that component's error rendering, or any provider requirement it gains, could silently break the retired-metric guard contract without a diagnostic failure pointing at `DynamicWidget`.
findings.recommendation: Change the mock path to `'../../AnalyticsWidget'` so it resolves from `__tests__/` to `src/pages/analytics/components/AnalyticsWidget`, matching the module `DynamicWidget.tsx` actually imports.

findings.title: No integration test for settings-page redirect
findings.problem: No test file navigates to `/settings/administration/ai-adoption-config` and asserts the URL settles at `/settings/administration`. The grep and glob search confirms zero references to this path in any test file; the two existing settings integration tests cover unrelated routes.
findings.impact: A regression in the loader route — an accidental deletion, a path typo, or a future router refactor — would produce a blank screen or 404 for users with bookmarked adoption-config URLs without any automated test failing.
findings.recommendation: Add an integration test using `renderPage('/settings/administration/ai-adoption-config')` (or the project's equivalent router harness) that asserts the settled URL is `/settings/administration` after navigation resolves.

findings.title: Commit subject violates enforced uppercase pattern
findings.problem: The commit `EPMCDME-14466: add planning artifacts` begins its description with the lowercase word 'add'. The project's enforced Tekton regex `^(EPMCDME)-(?!0+)\d+:\s[A-Z][a-z]*.*` requires the first character after the ticket prefix and space to be uppercase.
findings.impact: Tekton CI validates every commit subject in the review range against this pattern and blocks the pipeline on violations; this commit will fail the gate and prevent merging.
findings.recommendation: Reword the commit subject to `EPMCDME-14466: Add planning artifacts` (capitalise 'Add'), either via interactive rebase or a fixup commit before merge.
